foods.title: Traditional Foods
foods.subtitle: Beloved dishes of the Zulu people (ukudla kwesiZulu)

items.name: Crumbly Maize Porridge
items.desc: Dry, crumbly maize meal porridge. Often served with milk, amasi, beans, meat, or curry.
items.infoBoxText: A daily staple that provides the primary source of carbohydrates in the traditional diet.

items.name: Steamed Bread
items.desc: Traditional steamed bread usually served with meat stews.
items.infoBoxText: Cooked by steaming rather than baking, making it soft, dense, and perfect for soaking up rich gravies.

items.name: Pumpkin Porridge
items.desc: A sweet pumpkin and maize meal porridge.
items.infoBoxText: A naturally sweet, comforting dish that blends seasonal vegetables with maize.

items.name: Soft Maize Porridge
items.desc: Soft maize porridge eaten for breakfast or supper.
items.infoBoxText: A smooth, comforting porridge that starts or ends the day in many households.

items.name: Maize / Corn
items.desc: One of the most important traditional crops and food sources.
items.infoBoxText: The foundational ingredient for many Zulu dishes, from phuthu to umqombothi.

items.name: Taro Root
items.desc: Root vegetable boiled, roasted, or mashed.
items.infoBoxText: A highly nutritious indigenous root crop that thrives in the wet, humid climates of KZN.

items.name: Fermented Sour Milk
items.desc: Fermented sour milk. One of the most loved Zulu foods.
items.infoBoxText: Rich in probiotics, amasi is traditionally prepared in a calabash (igula).

items.name: Fermented Maize Beverage
items.desc: A nutritious fermented maize beverage.
items.infoBoxText: A non-alcoholic, energy-boosting drink popular among workers and families.

items.name: Sorghum Beer
items.desc: Traditional beer used during ceremonies and celebrations.
items.infoBoxText: Brewed over several days, it is essential for communicating with ancestors during rituals.

items.name: Cooked Beans
items.desc: Cooked beans often eaten with phuthu.
items.infoBoxText: A primary source of plant-based protein in the traditional diet.

items.name: Bambara Groundnuts
items.desc: Traditional indigenous beans.
items.infoBoxText: Highly drought-resistant and incredibly nutritious, often boiled and eaten as a snack.

items.name: Bread and Beans
items.desc: Popular household meal consisting of steamed bread and hearty beans.
items.infoBoxText: A beloved combination that is filling and affordable.

items.name: Beef Dishes
items.desc: Prepared in many traditional ways. Cattle hold immense wealth and spiritual value.
items.infoBoxText: Cattle are slaughtered primarily for significant cultural rituals and celebrations.

items.name: Goat Meat
items.desc: Common during ceremonies and ancestral rituals.
items.infoBoxText: Goats are deeply tied to ancestral communication (ukubika).

items.name: Traditional Chicken
items.desc: Traditional free range chicken dishes, often boiled until tough meat is tender.
items.infoBoxText: Zulu hard body chicken (umqhele) is prized for its rich, authentic flavor.

items.name: Cow's Head
items.desc: A respected traditional delicacy, traditionally reserved for the men of the homestead.
items.infoBoxText: Boiled until tender, it is a prized cut shared among elders and men.

items.name: Tripe / Intestines
items.desc: Prepared with spices or traditional seasonings.
items.infoBoxText: Cleaned thoroughly and slow-cooked, it is a favorite communal dish.

items.name: Trotters
items.desc: Cow or sheep trotters, slow cooked until tender and gelatinous.
items.infoBoxText: Requires hours of simmering to extract the rich flavors and tenderize the meat.

items.name: Oxtail
items.desc: Popular festive dish made from the tail of cattle.
items.infoBoxText: A rich, hearty stew usually enjoyed during big family gatherings.

items.name: Liver
items.desc: Often cooked with onions and spices.
items.infoBoxText: One of the first parts of the animal to be cooked and eaten during a slaughter.

items.name: Braaied Meat / Shisanyama
items.desc: Meat roasted over open coals, served at celebrations and gatherings.
items.infoBoxText: A cornerstone of modern and traditional social gatherings.

items.name: Traditional Wild Spinach
items.desc: General term for traditional leafy greens foraging in the wild.
items.infoBoxText: Packed with vitamins and iron, typically cooked with a little maize meal.

items.name: Wild Amaranth
items.desc: A nutritious indigenous vegetable gathered from the wild.
items.infoBoxText: Cooked like spinach, it provides essential nutrients to the traditional diet.

items.name: Pigweed
items.desc: One of the most common traditional leafy vegetables.
items.infoBoxText: Gathered in the summer months and cooked as a relish.

items.name: Maize and Greens Mash
items.desc: Popular leafy vegetable cooked directly into maize meal to form a tasty mash.
items.infoBoxText: A very common and filling way to consume healthy imifino.

items.name: Groundnut Veggie
items.desc: Cooked as a vegetable dish.
items.infoBoxText: A robust traditional crop that is boiled and seasoned.

items.name: Natal Plum
items.desc: A sweet, tart, bright red indigenous fruit.
items.infoBoxText: Gathered from thorny bushes, rich in Vitamin C.

items.name: Wild Berries
items.desc: Wild berries gathered seasonally from the veld.
items.infoBoxText: A sweet summer treat commonly foraged by herd boys.

items.name: Marula Fruit
items.desc: Consumed fresh or fermented into a potent alcoholic beverage.
items.infoBoxText: A highly valued fruit tree across Southern Africa.

items.name: Water Berry
items.desc: Traditional wild fruit from the Umdoni tree, turning dark purple when ripe.
items.infoBoxText: Sweet and slightly astringent, heavily favored by both people and birds.

items.name: Boiled Maize Kernels
items.desc: Whole maize kernels boiled until soft, often mixed with beans.
items.infoBoxText: A hardy, filling snack often packed for long journeys or days in the fields.

items.name: Dried Maize Snack
items.desc: A traditional filling meal or snack made of dried mealies.
items.infoBoxText: Requires a strong jaw but is incredibly satisfying and long-lasting.

items.name: Thick Maize Bread
items.desc: A thick maize meal preparation cooked with milk or vegetables.
items.infoBoxText: A hearty, dense staple that provides lasting energy.

items.name: Ceremonial Meat
items.desc: Prepared during weddings, umemulo, and family gatherings.
items.infoBoxText: Meats are often shared in a specific order according to status and gender.
